result.title: Pretty Linear Liars: Unregularized Probes Favor Intervention-Unfaithful Features
result.comment: 13 pages, 9 figures. Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Interpretability as a Science (InterpScience)
result.summary: Linear probing is a common technique in mechanistic interpretability despite the fact that the decodability of a given feature does not necessarily imply the network uses that feature. Intervention faithfulness, not merely decodability, is the appropriate criterion for whether a feature serves a defined active role in the model. Meanwhile, probe regularization has been used for feature discovery, but the impact of regularization on feature causality remains unclear. We study probe regularization systematically, starting with unregularized ordinary least squares (OLS) regression and considering increasing amounts of regularization via ridge regression. We show theoretically that OLS probes amplify low-variance directions in activation space that have spurious correlations with the target feature, whereas regularization reduces influence from these directions. Empirically, we find in a toy transformer and Llama-2-7B that intervention faithfulness increases up to a point, and then decreases again, and that the optimal regularization strength leads to features bearing striking similarity (in both direction and variance) to those learned by optimizing for intervention outcomes directly. Together, these results provide mechanistic justification for regularizing regression probes.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文系统研究线性探针正则化对干预忠实性的影响：理论上说明无正则 OLS 探针会放大与目标特征存在伪相关的低方差方向，并在 toy transformer 与 Llama-2-7B 上发现忠实性随正则强度先升后降，最优强度下的特征接近直接针对干预结果优化所得。
